clue.text: Lots in police will get backing to be forceful

indicators.note: getting backing means the whole assembled piece is turned round and read backwards
in says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
lots means many

explanation.surface: A report that plenty of officers in the force are being supported so they can act decisively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get backing' reads like police receiving support, but it turns the whole container round. The definition 'be forceful' stands loosely for an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone energetic and powerful in action is described as forceful.

clue.text: Plan to remove authorisation?

parts.note: the prefix de- means to remove or undo, as in defrost
to sign something is to give it authorisation

explanation.surface: A question about whether a scheme exists to strip someone of permission.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a made-up verb, the answer would mean 'take away the signature', a whimsical reading signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scheme or drawing prepared in advance is a plan.

clue.text: A bishop comes in at this time, tight

indicators.note: comes in says the bishop piece enters the middle of the time phrase

parts.note: at this time means now
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop arrives at the moment things are tense or cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tight space or margin is a slim, restricted one.

clue.text: One on the bench taking millions is a target for abuse

indicators.note: abuse means mistreatment, so the letters of these words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A corrupt court official pocketing millions becomes the object of public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just attaches M to the front of the rearranged IS A TARGET (AGISTRATE).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lay justice sitting on a court bench hears cases, so the bench phrase describes this official.

clue.text: Consider initially what could get cut in professorial role?

indicators.note: initially says take just the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: hair is what gets cut at the barber's

explanation.surface: Pondering which academic post might be axed in budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could get cut' sounds like university funding cuts but describes a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a chair, the named post an academic holds in a university department.

clue.text: Drink left for set of fans

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drink is left out for a crowd of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'remaining' but is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective sense: a team's following or body of backers is its fan base.

clue.text: Calculated work for a mathematician — or a judge

definitions.meaning: adding up figures, totalling a column, is mathematical work
a judge's closing review of the evidence for the jury has this name

explanation.surface: Totting up a sum might be a job for an academic or a courtroom official.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: totalling numbers, and the judge's concluding address to a jury before it retires.

clue.text: Refined tempo shortened? Not altogether

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Musing on whether a cultured performance is a slower or faster pace, but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone upper-class and elegant is called refined, smart or genteel.

clue.text: Creative test to be entered by one with spirit

indicators.note: being entered by means the first piece has the others placed inside it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An imaginative exam that a single spirited person sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inventive, novel work is creative, not copied from anything.

clue.text: Article on riots disturbed ideologue

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A news story about unrest upset a political zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a person devoted to an abstract doctrine or system of ideas is a thinker of that kind.

clue.text: Some Spanish ruggedly showing sign of indifference

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some Spaniards are toughly unconcerned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb-and-noun phrase standing in for the noun: a gesture of indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: raising the shoulders is the classic gesture meaning one does not care.

clue.text: It's a crime to disband guarantor of peace?

indicators.note: disbanding breaks up a group, so these letters are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: A claim that breaking up an army or band is criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce, ceasefire agreement ending fighting, secures peace, hence the question mark for this loose description.

clue.text: Suitable pressure to produce commercial vehicle

parts.note: good can mean suitable, fit for purpose
strain means pressure or stress

explanation.surface: The right amount of pressure is needed to make a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a freight railway train carries merchandise for trade, so it is a commercial vehicle.

clue.text: Stand holding up someone that's pegged out — alcohol's mentioned

definitions.text: Stand holding up someone that's pegged out

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the word sounds like the drink

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A rack supports someone who has collapsed drunk, with drink brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pegged out' is British slang for died.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame on which a coffin or corpse is set before burial supports a dead person.

clue.text: Cricketer turned wrong'un around start of play

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off

indicators.note: around says the sinner piece wraps the next letter

parts.note: a wrong'un is a bad person, a sinner

indicators.note: start of means take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bowler sends down a wrong'un, a googly, as play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: A wrong'un is also cricket slang for a googly, which breaks the opposite way to a leg-break, hence the misleading cricket surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bowler who spins the ball from the off side is a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Fantastic age for a firm's dairy product

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wildly altered, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A company has a remarkable period with its milk-based goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of firm's supplies a letter S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft fresh French cheese is one of the products of a dairy.

clue.text: Fellows, volunteers, switched on with variable way of thinking

parts.note: fellows are men
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a light switched on is lit
Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Men and volunteers, made alert, bring a changeable attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a characteristic mindset or attitude is one's way of thinking.

clue.text: Curious case comes before 'father of French adventure'

indicators.note: comes before says the rearranged piece is placed in front
curious means odd, so the letters are oddly rearranged

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
de is the French for of

explanation.surface: An odd matter predates a French priest's adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a reckless or mischievous exploit is a kind of adventure.

clue.text: Following a service, abbreviated bit of applause one milks, perhaps

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
RM, Royal Marines, is an abbreviated armed service
giving someone a hand is a round of applause

explanation.surface: After a church service, a short clap for someone who milks cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a labourer on a farm may do the milking among other chores.

clue.text: Skill required in smart job — competitive opening?

indicators.note: required in says the skill piece is needed inside the next word

parts.note: to smart is to sting
art means skill
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Talent is needed in a sharp career move at a rival firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The place a race begins from is where a contest opens, hence the question mark for this playful phrasing.

clue.text: Element underpinning start of joint talk for specialists?

indicators.note: underpinning in a down clue puts the element beneath the other piece
start of means take the opening letter of the word

parts.note: argon is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A chemical element at the root of a shared lecture for experts.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: technical terminology used within a profession is talk only specialists follow.

clue.text: Small vessel in artistic work

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A little boat appears in a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rough drawing is a piece of art.

clue.text: Military force mad to lose leader

indicators.note: losing its leader means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: An unhinged army loses its commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a land fighting body of soldiers is a military force.

clue.text: Bright person touring a remote island venue for game

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the bright person surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a bright spark is a clever person; spark alone serves
remote means far

explanation.surface: A clever traveller visits a distant island to play a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means wild animals, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild animals are called game, and an enclosure where visitors drive among them is a place for them.

clue.text: After a time, credit's cut short in storage site?

indicators.note: after says the credit piece follows the first pieces
cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: on tick means on credit; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: After a while, someone's credit is curtailed at a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter of TICK, leaving TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the roof space of a house is often used for keeping things.

clue.text: Indelible mark in cliff

definitions.meaning: a lasting mark on skin left by a healed wound
a steep rocky crag or cliff face

explanation.surface: A permanent stain on a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lasting mark from a wound, and a steep rocky outcrop.

clue.text: One for whom no order is welcome?

definitions.text: One for whom no order is welcome?

parts.words: One for whom no order is welcome
parts.note: someone who rejects government and wants no social order at all

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes being given instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no order' looks like refusing commands but means the absence of a governing system.
explanation.definitionFit: Political sense: a believer in abolishing government welcomes the absence of order.

clue.text: Report of man that's stood by castle in dark period

indicators.note: report of means the sound of a spoken word

parts.note: a knight is a chess man that stands next to the castle (rook) at the start

explanation.surface: News of a guard posted beside a castle during a gloomy time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the hours of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Grey metal workman heading off with lorry, discontented

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a welder joins metal

indicators.note: discontented means the contents are emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A grey metalworker drives off in a lorry, unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' leaves the outer letters LY of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey-haired people are old, so grey describes the aged.

clue.text: Bit round river? This is unseen in Greek city

indicators.note: round says the coin piece encloses the river letter

parts.note: a bit is a coin, as in a threepenny bit

indicators.note: unseen says the word is is removed from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin near a river may be invisible in a Greek town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unseen' removes IS from THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ancient Greek city known from Paul's letters to the people there.
